# Compost bins

Two wooden bins stand at the bottom of the plot. Kitchen scraps, peelings and grass cuttings go in the first; every few weeks I turn the heap into the second bin to let it breathe. Waste that was destined for the bin slowly decomposes into dark, crumbly nutrients that feed the beds in spring.

The balance matters: greens give nitrogen, browns such as cardboard and dry leaves give carbon, and a handful of soil brings the organisms. If the heap smells, add browns and turn it. If it is dry, water it. A full cycle takes about a year, and nothing in the garden grows better than what the compost has fed.

Spread it thinly in March and leave the worms to do the rest.
